Subject: Headroom renewal: headroom-swap + safety buffer proposal

Hi Simon / Headroom procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — appreciate the transparency on expected growth patterns for Q3–Q4. Based on what you shared, we put together a short operational proposal that aims to: 1) preserve a full 12-month price hold at current rates, 2) give you committed headroom that flexes with actual usage, and 3) offer contingency credits if usage spikes beyond the headroom corridor.

High level (attached: Headroom_Term_Swap_v1.pdf + MAP_Headroom_2027-06.xlsx):
- Year 1: Convert your retainer to a measured capacity commit for core services (equivalent to ~70% of prior run rate). We hold today's unit price for 12 months.
- Headroom swap: We allocate a 20% headroom pool that is billed monthly at a reduced uplift rate; unused headroom rolls into a true-up credit at renewal.
- Contingency credits: For any month where usage exceeds headroom by >25%, Redwood provides a one-time credit equal to 10% of that month's overage (applied at invoice). This is to reduce operational shock while preserving economics.
- Invoicing & true-up cadence: Monthly invoices; annual reconciliation with true-up credits; option to convert rolled credits into one-time compute credits for burst.

Ask: Can you confirm procurement is comfortable with monthly invoicing + annual true-up? If so we’ll prepare a clean addendum and a short mutual action plan to get legal/finance sign-off.

Next steps we propose:
1) Procurement thumbs-up to the headroom mechanics (this email)
2) Redwood sends redline-ready addendum + MAP (timeline: 48 hours)
3) Headroom legal/finance review & sign (target: 7–10 business days)

I’ve copied Ben (Sales Ops) and Karthik (RevOps) to coordinate the MAP and billing details. Attaching a draft MAP and the term-swap summary for your review.

Thanks,

Markus Klein | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear proposal. A few clarifying Qs from our side:

1) On the headroom pool — is the reduced uplift billed at a fixed per-token/per-embed rate or a percent-of-list uplift? We need line-item detail for our cost model.
2) True-up credits: are these automatically applied on the invoice or do we request them at reconciliation? Our finance team prefers automatic line-item credits where possible.
3) Contingency credit timing: if a June spike triggers a 10% credit, do we see that reflected on the July invoice?

Procurement is generally open to the mechanics but finance wants to see the exact invoicing rows. If you can provide a one-page invoice mock that maps the components (commit, headroom billed, overage, credit), that will speed internal approval.

Also: we have a delivery milestone in August tied to a pilot expansion; if that ramps, we may exceed headroom in Q3. Would Redwood consider a phased increase to the committed baseline mid-year (with pro-rata crediting) so we don’t have to do a mid-cycle true-up later?

Simon
Simon Lee
Head of Cloud Ops | Headroom Technologies
simon.lee@headroomtech.com

Simon — good questions, thank you. Quick answers + next-deliverables below.

1) Headroom billing: billed as a reduced per-unit rate (we will provide exact per-token/per-embed figures in the invoice mock). For the MAP we used a 12% uplift to illustrate the math; we can surface a per-unit table in the invoice mock.
2) True-up credits: automatic line-item credit on the invoice during reconciliation (Finance friendly). We’ll mark these as "True-up credit (rolled headroom)" so the ledger is explicit.
3) Credit timing: yes — a qualifying overage in June is reflected as a credit on the July invoice. We’ll call this out in the billing notes.

Phased baseline increase: we can support a mid-year committed baseline bump with pro-rata billing and a matching pro-rata reduction in the headroom pool. That avoids a large true-up and preserves price hold for the remainder of the term. If that works, we’ll include a simple clause in the addendum: "Customer may request one committed baseline increase per 12-month term; Redwood will apply pro-rata billing and adjust headroom accordingly."

Deliverables (I’ll own):
- Invoice mock with line items and example months (attached to next email) — Ben will draft.
- Clean addendum + MAP for signature (Redwood legal + your procurement) — include phased baseline clause.
- DocuSign envelope for signature if procurement prefers e-sign.

Ben / Karthik / Lauren — can you assemble the invoice mock and the addendum redline? Target: Ben to send invoice mock within 24 hours; legal redline within 48 hrs.

Cheers,

Markus
